correctness.rationale: The unique-path identity yields the p and p^2 coefficients of both outbreak moments. First-order one-edge failure yields the Wiener-index coefficient at p=1. A 2(n-1)-coordinate finite-difference derivative bound gives absolute p^3 and (1-p)^2 remainders sufficiently small throughout the displayed common intervals. The wedge extremizers follow from the degree sum; Wiener extrema follow from edge cuts and leaf-removal induction. Exact finite Prüfer-sequence enumeration tested 1,437 labeled trees of orders 4–6, all bond states, both endpoint coefficients, inequalities inside the explicit intervals, and the quartic for n=4. Enumeration is corroborative rather than the basis of the all-order result.

originality.rationale: The main all-order claim concerns opposite unique extremal trees and uniform transmission neighborhoods, not the known formulas for a path or star. The open full text of Moore–Newman (arXiv:cond-mat/9911492) concerns small-world networks and their epidemic percolation threshold. The complete 2021 Lanchier–La Salle arXiv:2111.01982 explicitly restricts its moment bounds to finite regular graphs, while citing the distinct 2020 path/ring/star calculation. Wang arXiv:0709.1679 concerns Wiener-index tree extrema, which are acknowledged as classical ingredients. The directly relevant Jevtić–Lanchier–La Salle 2020 article was read only at abstract level because a full authorized copy was unavailable; its coverage of an all-tree endpoint theorem therefore remains a specific residual risk. Searches of published mathematical records returned no statement of the all-tree variance switch. No independence or exhaustive novelty certification is inferred from search failure.
residual_risks: Full text of doi:10.1016/j.spl.2020.108714 could not be inspected despite public preprint/OA search and authorized institutional attempt. It might contain an all-tree comparison not revealed by the abstract.

value.rationale: The all-order theorem isolates a genuine decision-relevant reversal in epidemic-size uncertainty under one fixed contact budget: star uniquely maximizes outbreak variance for weak transmissibility but uniquely minimizes it for near-certain transmissibility, with the path reversing roles. The two different invariants give a structural explanation and the same explicit endpoint window works across all tree topologies. This is more than a single computed example or an unrelated metric comparison; it identifies qualitative regime-dependent global design optimizers. The model assumptions and lack of intermediate-regime classification are declared.
